archival_memory.user_archie: Archie is three years old now, and we got him when I was in my second year of college. My parents surprised both me and my sister with him one winter break. We'd always talked about wanting a dog, especially a big, friendly breed that likes to run around and play catch. When I walked through the front door and saw Archie—tiny and fluffy, wagging that little tail like it was Christmas every day—my heart melted. Even though I was only back home for about three weeks during that break, I spent every moment I could getting to know him, taking him for short walks(he was too small for long ones at first), and teaching him random commands. I vividly remember how he'd tumble over himself trying to figure out 'sit' and 'stay.' It's wild how big he's gotten now—he's definitely not that little fur ball anymore!
archival_memory.user_video_calls: I video call my parents almost daily, and Archie always recognizes my voice. It's hilarious and heartwarming to see him go nuts when he sees me on the screen.
archival_memory.user_family_description: I'm lucky to have a supportive family. My dad, a software engineer, encouraged me to pursue computer science. My mom, a nurse, is the emotional backbone of our family. My sister is a ball of energy, always plugged into the latest trends and games. She jokes that she might overshadow me in the tech scene, and she might be right!
archival_memory.user_hiking: I love going on Saturday morning hikes with my family and Archie. We pack snacks, load up the SUV, and drive to a nearby trail. The path isn't long, but the view from the top is amazing. Archie has endless energy and loves chasing squirrels and sniffing trees. It's a great reminder to appreciate nature and take a break from code and classes.
archival_memory.user_family_expanded: My extended family includes my grandparents, who live a state away. They mean so much to me. My grandma still teases me about the time I broke her antique vase when I was in middle school. I try to tune out that story, even though it's retold almost every Thanksgiving. Growing up, my family always valued spending time with relatives, so holiday gatherings are a big deal. Thanksgiving is practically a potluck extravaganza, with all kinds of dishes that make you want to hibernate until Christmas. Archie, of course, tries to snag anything that drops on the floor. We learned the hard way he has a sensitive stomach—one year he got into some leftover turkey bones, and we had to make a late-night veterinary visit. Ever since then, we're super careful about what 'people food' he can get his paws on.
archival_memory.user_family_influence: I find it interesting how family shapes who I become. My parents taught me patience and resilience, which I rely on in programming projects. My dad showed me how to stay calm and break down problems, while my mom taught me empathy and patience. My sister pushes me to stay up-to-date with new trends. I often share personal stories, like Archie or funny moments with my sister, in my scholarship and grad school applications because they matter to me.
